comparator.name: Art History (Kunstgeschiedenis)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 OER and current student curriculum define a 180-EC bachelor: a 120-EC major and 60-EC profiling space. The major contains two compulsory first-year basic packages (60 EC), two compulsory context courses (15 EC), one 30-EC depth package, and a 15-EC final paper. The target does not choose between the two formal depth packages, so the first package in the OER, Kunst en architectuur tot 1850, is instantiated by the official-order tie-break. The 60-EC profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor, exchange or internship.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized Kunstgeschiedenis target does not select between the two formal 30-EC depth packages. The adopted 2026–2027 OER lists Kunst en architectuur tot 1850 before Moderne en hedendaagse kunst en architectuur, so the former is selected by official order, before and independently of UCR course selection. The 60-EC profiling space remains open because the OER does not prescribe one subject.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad art-history response owns the eight direct programme interests. Each of Utrecht’s two formal depth packages supplies an independently evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible related direction. Their schedules differ from the broad programme by at least 30 EC and from each other by substantially more. Production stops because three UCR alternatives is the permitted maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: PPD provides broad academic development; Utrecht’s course is specifically an introduction to art-historical research.
Both introduce Western art history and visual interpretation; UCR begins with the Renaissance rather than antiquity.
Both analyse how cultural objects are made and interpreted through material evidence; UCR approaches this through archaeology.
UCR directly studies Renaissance painting, sculpture and architecture within Mediterranean exchange.
African Art & Heritage provides a substantive global and postcolonial art-history perspective with object research.
Both directly address modern and contemporary art; UCR emphasises museum display and interpretation.
Heritage & Ancient Democracy examines how material and architectural heritage is interpreted and used in the present.
Both examine art-historical methods, historiography, visual analysis and scholarly writing.
UCR offers ancient, Renaissance and modern material, but no selected course reproduces this dedicated late-antique and medieval survey.
No selected UCR course reproduces the comparator’s object-to-urban-scale architectural sequence.
UCR addresses architecture within art history and archaeology but lacks a dedicated pre-1850 architectural-history methods course.
UCR has no selected location-based Renaissance field course equivalent to the Florence excursion.
Global perspectives appear across UCR courses, but no single selected course reproduces this compulsory global-art context component.
World Myth & Literature studies the transfer of mythic narratives into images across cultures, supporting iconographic interpretation.
Both require sustained independent source-based research and argument; the UCR seminar is historical and smaller than the art-history thesis.
The genuine 60-EC profiling space is preserved without inventing a minor, exchange or internship.

notes.text: Utrecht provides a structured 120-EC art-history major with eight foundation courses, a formal four-course depth package, global and heritage context, and a 15-EC art-history final paper. UCR offers a smaller art-history and heritage sequence supported by archaeology, history, literature, media and cultural analysis; it does not reproduce the full specialist sequence, dedicated architectural-history progression or compulsory art-history thesis.
